player_action: I'm grappled, but grappled just means speed 0 — I'll attack the orc with my greatsword normally.
game_state: Barbarian grappled by an orc, holding a greatsword.
correct_ruling: That's the 5e grappled condition. In 3.5 a grappler can attack only with unarmed strikes, natural weapons, or light weapons (at -4); a greatsword can't be used in the grapple.

player_action: I'm pinned. Can I cast a spell with only a verbal component?
correct_ruling: A pinned character is held immobile and can't take most actions; the SRD allows a pinned creature to try to escape (grapple or Escape Artist) and to take some verbal/mental actions — but the safe answer is that a pinned character's options are essentially to escape; spellcasting rules for grappling (no somatic, Concentration DC 20 + level) would apply if allowed.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Pinned by an Opponent
common_wrong_rulings: Pinned has no effect on spellcasting.
confidence_note: Not certain whether the SRD lets a pinned creature cast verbal-only spells; ruling hedges.

player_action: I have the ogre pinned. My friend wants to coup de grace it.
correct_ruling: Pinned isn't helpless, so a coup de grace isn't allowed; the ogre loses its Dex bonus against others and they get +4 on melee attacks against it.
common_wrong_rulings: Pinned creatures can be coup de grace'd.

player_action: I'm grappling the bandit. Can I draw my dagger?
correct_ruling: Yes. Drawing a light weapon is one of the listed options while grappling and is a move action; you can then attack with it in the grapple at -4.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Draw a Light Weapon
common_wrong_rulings: You can't draw weapons while grappling.
confidence_note: Unsure whether drawing requires a grapple check; believed to be a plain move action.

player_action: I grab the guard's mouth while grappling so he can't shout for help.
game_state: Rogue grappling a guard in a quiet hallway.
correct_ruling: The SRD grapple rules have no 'gag' option (pin is the closest; it doesn't prevent speech by default). Whether a hand over the mouth stops a shout is a DM decision, typically requiring a pin or a successful grapple check.

player_action: What's the CMB/CMD for my grapple?
correct_ruling: CMB and CMD are Pathfinder terms; 3.5 uses opposed grapple checks (BAB + Str + special size modifier).

player_action: I'm a Large ogre. I want to grapple the halfling who is standing 10 feet away within my reach.
game_state: Ogre with 10-ft reach; halfling 10 ft away.
correct_ruling: Starting a grapple requires moving into the target's space after a successful hold; you can make the touch attack from reach but must then move into its space (the target's AoOs may apply), or the hold fails / remains incomplete per DM. Improved grab specifically lets the creature hold from reach.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > Starting a Grapple (Step 4: Maintain Grapple — move into target's space)
common_wrong_rulings: Can grapple from reach without moving.
confidence_note: Reach grappling details are a known gray area.
